bull_bear.body: Debt-free balance sheet (D/E 0.18%). No immediate fundraising plans. Dividend declaration delayed but expected within weeks. Focus on organic growth funding via internal accruals.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Vadhvan Port project delays (undefined timeline); Government payment cycles (state treasury issues vs. central reliability); Commodity inflation exceeding escalation clauses; Execution risk on record order book with limited idle TBM capacity; Dependency on Adani Group for ~40% of pipeline.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Highly confident on order momentum and execution capabilities; transparent about one-off nature of Q4 margins; cautious on timing of tender conversions despite large pipeline; emphasized 'no legacy jobs' and clean balance sheet.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Data Center vertical already scaled to INR 3,000 Cr order book quietly within group; 90% of mobilization advances (INR 1,400 Cr total) are interest-free, improving working capital efficiency; TBM asset turnover is critical bottleneck with zero idle capacity.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Balance sheet deleveraged materially over the cycle — net debt to EBITDA fell from 1.27x in FY19 to 0.44x in FY26 as EBITDA scaled from ₹463 Cr to ₹1,199 Cr.
- Credit ratings upgraded to A+ (Stable) by both CARE and ICRA in March 2026 after six years at A, citing ~30% revenue CAGR, order-book visibility, the ownership change and execution track record.
- Capital base strengthened to ₹2,400 Cr net worth (FY26) against ₹1,001 Cr borrowings and ₹475 Cr cash, with returns of 34% RoCE and 28% RoE in FY26.
- Asset base remains working-capital heavy rather than fixed-asset heavy — ₹5,631 Cr of current assets versus ₹1,456 Cr non-current assets on a ₹7,087 Cr balance sheet in FY26.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Metro/Tunneling: Completed Bangalore, Mumbai, Udangudi; ongoing Chennai (4 TBMs deployed, 40% work left, completion 2028), Delhi, Pune. Marine: Vadhvan Port delayed (local issues), breakwater/dredging tenders pending. Data Centers: New division, 3-4 jobs secured from Adani Group (INR 3,000 Cr), focusing on group opportunities (e.g., Vizag). Roads: New Bihar elevated corridor (self-executed).
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Capacity constraints in tunneling and marine EPC as order book hits record highs | NBCC (India) Ltd | beneficiary | Low | Potential subcontracting partner if Cemindia faces TBM bottlenecks, though Cemindia prefers self-execution. |
| Inflationary pressure on steel/cement impacting marginal EPC players without escalation clauses | Small-cap Civil Contractors | loser | Med | Cemindia's 80% clause coverage highlights vulnerability of smaller peers lacking pricing power. |
| Need for specialized data center construction as digital infra capex surges | Adani Enterprises Ltd | beneficiary | High | Parent company driving order flow to Cemindia for data centers; synergies benefit both entities. |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Presents itself as a major Indian infrastructure player with ~9 decades of execution history across marine, metro rail, airports, industrial structures and buildings.
- Footprint spans 16 Indian states plus three overseas locations (UAE, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka), with 98% of the order book in India and 2% overseas.
- Client mix is deliberately spread across Government (~10%), PSU (~27%) and Private (~63%) with 30+ diversified clients, which the deck frames as reducing client concentration risk.
- Positions the Adani Group association as a strategic moat — operational synergies from shared resources and vendor network, access to the group's project pipeline in India and overseas, and governance/brand leverage.
- Frames the opportunity around India's infrastructure megatrend: ₹12.22 lakh Cr Union Budget capex (4.4% of GDP, highest ever, 6x since FY14), ₹111 lakh Cr NIP/Gati Shakti pipeline and urbanisation rising to 50% by 2047.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Rebrand] The company has been renamed Cemindia Projects Limited, formerly ITD Cementation India Limited, and now trades under the NSE symbol CEMPRO / BSE code 509496.
- [Ownership] A change of ownership into the Adani ecosystem is cited by the rating agencies as a driver of growth synergies and stronger financial flexibility.
- [Board] Leadership is Adani-linked and newly configured — Malay Mahadevia as Chairman, Jayanta Basu as Managing Director (39+ years), with independent directors Manoj Kumar Kohli, Sangeeta Bhatia and Abizer Diwanji.
- [Governance] Three additional non-statutory committees have been created — IT & Data Security, Corporate Responsibility, and Legal, Regulatory & Tax.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Q4 margin (15.1%) boosted by INR 100 Cr claims and provision reversals; sustainable guidance reset to 10.5%. Cost escalation protection exists in ~80% of contracts (escalation clauses/star rates), but abnormal inflation (war/commodity spikes) remains a risk. Subcontracting minimal for key new road jobs.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: 25% for FY27; Margin: 10.5% sustainable EBITDA margin (excluding other income/one-offs); Order Inflow Target: INR 25,000 Cr for FY27; Capex: INR 350-400 Cr for FY27.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Total INR 29,000 Cr includes INR 1,600 Cr (L1 pending LoA) and INR 3,200 Cr (secured in April). Key wins: Delhi Metro Underground, Pune Metro, Kolkata Metro, JSW Port, Abu Dhabi overseas job, Bihar elevated road. Data Center segment contributes ~INR 3,000 Cr. Legacy low-margin jobs fully exited.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Pipeline of INR 70,000 Cr (35-40% from Adani Group). Major opportunities in large-diameter tunnels (market >INR 1 Lakh Cr), highways (market ~INR 1 Lakh Cr), and potential Navi Mumbai Airport Phase 2 bid. Data center civil works emerging as high-growth vertical within group ecosystem.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Cemindia crossed INR 10,000 Cr revenue with a 66% YoY EBITDA jump in Q4 driven by one-off claim realizations, while securing a record INR 19,000 Cr orders to expand the book to INR 29,000 Cr. Guidance points to 25% revenue growth in FY27, underpinned by a massive INR 70,000 Cr pipeline and new verticals like data centers, though sustainable margins are guided lower at 10.5% excluding one-offs.

open.item: Commodity/crude inflation flagged as a margin risk; ~30% jobs have star-price pass-through, others partial escalation clauses, some none (~80% jobs have some inflation protection).
Opportunity pipeline ~INR70,000 crores (~35-40% from group); roads/highways and tunnels each ~INR1 lakh cr market.
FY27 capex to be higher at ~INR350-400 crores (FY26 was ~INR260 cr).
Sustainable EBITDA margin (ex-other income) guided at ~10-10.5% going forward; Q4's 15.1%/12% boosted by one-time claims and provision reversals.
FY27 order inflow target ~INR25,000 crores (vs ~INR19,000 cr secured in FY26 incl L1/April).
FY27 revenue expected to grow at least 25% over FY26; ~20-25% for next 1-2 years.
Aim to derive around 30% of revenue from overseas in 2 to 3 years' time.
Chennai Metro (~40% value left, incl stations) expected to complete by end-2027/beginning-2028 (~mid 2028).
Aspiration to grow ~20-25% for the next ~3 years given strong Indian infrastructure cycle.
Dividend was not declared with results due to a process delay; to be declared within a few weeks.
No fundraising plan in the near future; comfortable with current funds.
Buying new TBMs for Pune Metro and Delhi Metro (Bangalore TBMs sold); large-diameter TBMs needed for large tunnel wins; no idle TBMs currently.
Vadhvan Port flagged as a slow-moving project delayed by local issues beyond company control; breakwater/dredging tenders pending customer release.
Intends to bid for Navi Mumbai Airport Phase 2 (large contract, potentially >INR10,000 cr) whenever it comes.
Political risk in overseas countries flagged as the main risk that could affect margins (e.g., Bangladesh, Colombo).
Labor shortage flagged for building/labor-oriented jobs causing some delays; mitigated via mechanization and workforce retention.
Management remains cautious on new Bangladesh orders, watching how the situation evolves.

verdicts.item: Organization geared to sustain ~25% growth with roughly same manpower/machinery base; plant/machinery buyable, knowledge is the key constraint.
verdicts.note: 20-25% growth reaffirmed, but 'If we have to do more job, we require more TBMs... We are buying new TBM for Pune Metro and Delhi Metro' - machinery being added, not same base.

verdicts.item: Ganga Expressway ~50% complete; expected to be substantially completed by June-July 2025.
verdicts.note: Analyst (uncorrected): 'Ganga Expressway we got commissioned' - substantially complete, past the Jun-Jul 2025 target.

verdicts.item: Capex ~INR67 crores this quarter; next year capex to be under control, lower investment than prior 2 years.
verdicts.note: 'Capex, INR260 crores... This is for the last year' - FY26 capex controlled versus earlier 450+ cr years.

verdicts.item: Adani becoming new owner expected to positively impact ITD, enabling more domestic and overseas work and portfolio diversification.
verdicts.note: 'with the push of our promoter, the futures are definitely going to be further better'; group data-center jobs and 'secured around INR14,000 crores' - Adani ownership impact materializing.

verdicts.item: Exploring new segments like data center, green/renewable energy, high-speed rail track laying, but no big presence yet.
verdicts.note: 'We have opened a new division. We have already secured 3 or 4 jobs from Adani Group... around INR3,000 crores' - data-center segment entered.

verdicts.item: Strategy to keep focusing on core strength marine, with airports, buildings, industrial structures as secondary priority.
verdicts.note: 'Marine is a limited market'; core marine (Vadhvan, Bangladesh) retained but roads/highways/tunnel now flagged as the main opportunities - focus broadening beyond marine.

verdicts.item: FY26 order inflow expected around INR12,000-13,000 crores (including new-promoter jobs).
verdicts.note: 'secured around INR14,000 crores of job, excluding the L1 and the job which was secured in April. Put together INR19,000 crores' - FY26 inflow beat the 12,000-13,000 guide.

verdicts.item: FY25 revenue expected to be close to INR10,000 crores.
verdicts.note: FY25 revenue 'INR9,246 crores' - near but ~7.5% below the 'close to INR10,000 crores' target. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: 20%-25% revenue growth guidance for next 2-3 years reaffirmed (ex-Bangladesh).
verdicts.note: 'Revenue should be at least 25% more than this year' for FY27, but FY26 actual growth only 9% - forward target intact, current year below. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: EBITDA margin expected to remain stable around 9.5%-10% going forward.
verdicts.note: FY26 margin 11.9%; 'It will be around 10% to 10.5% going forward' - at/above the stable 9.5-10% range.

verdicts.item: FY25 total capex to be INR120-125 crores at max (~INR100 cr done in 9M).
verdicts.note: expired: no update 4Q past horizon Q4FY25

verdicts.item: Adani open offer/acquisition transaction expected to complete by end March 2025 (pending SEBI approval and lender consents).
verdicts.note: 'formerly ITD Cementation India Limited', now part of Adani/'our promoter' - open offer/acquisition completed (after the Mar-2025 target).

wtt.summary: 74% guidance hit (21 chains); 3/8 projects on-time; 2 expired; 14% theme consistency (info)
wtt.tone_latest: Confident and buoyant; management transparently attributed the strong 15.1% Q4 EBITDA to one-time claims (INR150 cr FY, INR100 cr Q4) and provision reversals, guiding back to ~10.5% sustainable, and acknowledged the dividend delay and Vadhvan slippage.

meta.thesis: Cemindia crossed INR 10,000 Cr revenue with a 66% YoY EBITDA jump in Q4 driven by one-off claim realizations, while securing a record INR 19,000 Cr orders to expand the book to INR 29,000 Cr. Guidance points to 25% revenue growth in FY27, underpinned by a massive INR 70,000 Cr pipeline and new verticals like data centers, though sustainable margins are guided lower at 10.5% excluding one-offs.
